title: Advanced Next.js 16
summary: A hard front-end development path for experienced Next.js engineers covering rendering, caching, force-dynamic, invalidation, performance, and migration pain points in Next.js 16.
audience: Experienced Next.js App Router engineers who already ship production React applications and need hard-level caching, SSR, rendering, and migration judgment.

units.title: Rendering Model
units.summary: Model Server Components, streaming, request-time work, and Suspense boundaries in Next.js 16.

units.title: force-dynamic In Context
units.summary: Learn what force-dynamic meant before Cache Components and how to review it now.

units.title: Cache Components
units.summary: Use explicit cache scopes, lifetimes, tags, and keys for production-safe reuse.

units.title: Data Fetching And Caching
units.summary: Separate request memoization, persistent server cache, browser cache, and stale data contracts.

units.title: Invalidation And Mutations
units.summary: Connect Server Actions, updateTag, revalidateTag, and mutation correctness.

units.title: Production Pain Points
units.summary: Diagnose boundary bugs involving request APIs, client bundles, secrets, and stale cache state.

units.title: Performance Architecture
units.summary: Review Turbopack, routing, prefetching, streaming, and cache decisions as one performance system.

units.title: Migration Review
units.summary: Plan a Next.js 16 migration around behavior, rollout risk, and official upgrade paths.
